subject.title: Feature Request: Session rotation/archive lifecycle event for cron job triggers

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable session archive/rotation event that cron jobs can subscribe to, or should this workflow use existing plugin/internal hook surfaces instead?
rationale: Current main has adjacent session_end and compaction hooks but no cron event schedule, and the permanent choice affects cron schema, plugin/API boundaries, archived transcript privacy, and operator-visible automation semantics.

options.title: Design a cron lifecycle event
options.body: Add a scoped session archive/rotation event contract with explicit permissions, event_id traceability, metadata-only payloads, docs, and tests across compaction and reset/archive paths.

options.title: Bless plugin hooks instead
options.body: Document plugin session_end or internal hooks as the supported route for post-session automation and avoid a new cron schedule kind unless a concrete hook API gap remains.

options.title: Defer to memory lifecycle work
options.body: Keep this blocked on the related reset/session-memory lifecycle decisions and revisit cron triggering after those boundaries are stable.

recommendation.title: Design a cron lifecycle event
recommendation.body: Add a scoped session archive/rotation event contract with explicit permissions, event_id traceability, metadata-only payloads, docs, and tests across compaction and reset/archive paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined recent history across session reset identity and cron declaration surfaces that a durable lifecycle-event decision would touch.
